layer: L1.5 / TypeScript horizontal admission-handoff graph pattern
question: How should @graphrefly/ts hand a candidate from one hub into a downstream lifecycle only after an explicit correlated admission, without letting rejected, unmatched or non-occurring branches preflight that lifecycle or requiring call sites to patch partial and RESOLVED behavior?
decision: Add one future public TypeScript horizontal graph-pattern factory named admissionHandoff under @graphrefly/ts/patterns, not core, operators, solutions or extra. The pattern accepts normalized candidate and decision DATA carrying stable identity plus fingerprint; correlates candidate-before-decision and decision-before-candidate order; and exposes inspectable accepted, rejected, status, issues and bounded cursor outputs. Its accepted port is a quiet causal boundary: after activation, rejected, unmatched, duplicate-replay and fail-closed conflict paths produce no DIRTY, DATA or RESOLVED wave toward the downstream lifecycle; a newly admitted occurrence starts one fresh downstream DIRTY then DATA wave, with exact identity and fingerprint replay deduplicated. One candidate has at most one terminal decision; identity/fingerprint conflicts fail closed; pending and recent correlation state are explicitly bounded. Realize the boundary from existing pull semantics, deferred ctx.upNext(PULL), Graph retention and named nodes, state and dependencies so raw describe and Graph-native observation expose candidate, decision, correlation, release and accepted/rejected causality. The retained release controller is topology-owned; no WeakMap domain authority, external emitter, caller queue, raw async, timer, hidden fallback or manual call-site RESOLVED is permitted. Factory-internal lifecycle flags are fixed and not caller-overridable. Existing filter, valve and other operator flags remain unchanged globally; until a separately reviewed enforcement API exists, call sites must follow the disciplinary rule that they do not override those operators' factory-owned partial behavior or add partial/RESOLVED patches to compensate for a missing causal boundary. This pattern is the reusable default for admission-gated hub-to-hub lifecycle handoffs, including workflow stage gates, optional or technically excluded branches, retry/resource/capacity admission, capability/tool-run admission and Work Item-to-Memory-to-target transfer. It does not replace combine/zip/join snapshot semantics, pull/read models, feedback/state/rewire, unconditional transforms or cross-Graph wire bridges. Public promotion must prove F-NO-WEDGE-CUT with the Eval transfer path and at least one non-Eval consumer. No library source, package export, eval migration, implementation, protocol, conformance, cross-runtime change, compatibility path, provider access, live run or spend is authorized by this design lock.
rationale: Ordinary filter/valve dependencies may legitimately propagate a settlement preflight before knowing whether a value will be admitted. In the Eval's hub-to-hub boundary that preflight dirtied Work Item and Agentic Memory lifecycles that were not meant to start, leading to dozens of partial:true and explicit RESOLVED repairs. Those repairs weakened node contracts and moved settlement obligations across the topology instead of expressing the actual causal gate. A pull-quiet accepted port structurally withholds the downstream wave until correlated admission, so the affected patches disappear rather than being standardized. The existing wave protocol and pull/retention substrate are sufficient for this behavior; a named bounded graph pattern makes it reusable, inspectable and testable without a new protocol primitive. Limiting the claim to admission-gated lifecycle handoffs preserves the distinct semantics of joins, snapshots, feedback and wire bridges.
